title: Generating Module Documentation
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of Generating Module Documentation and define its core vocabulary.

content.intro: This lesson covers Generating Module Documentation in the PowerShell learning path. It expands the supplied syllabus heading into an actionable draft with a visual, a worked example, and a short knowledge check.
content.why_it_matters: Automated tests check behavior repeatedly; mocks isolate dependencies that are slow, external or unsafe. PSScriptAnalyzer provides static diagnostics but does not prove correctness, so combine tests, review, supported-version checks and reproducible release steps.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Review this snippet as a static teaching example. content_blocks.troubleshooting: Check command availability with Get-Command, inspect values with Get-Member, consult Get-Help -Full, and verify PowerShell version/platform before assuming identical output. Do not run examples that change system state without adapting and reviewing them.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet and use synthetic values. If you created test files, delete only those files within the dedicated practice folder after checking their paths.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety note
content_blocks.text: The main path targets modern PowerShell 7.6 LTS. Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility is labeled separately. Some providers, admin cmdlets and APIs depend on OS, module version, permissions or tenant access; the examples are static references, not proof of execution.

content.task: Try it yourself: design a reusable interface with explicit inputs and outputs. Use synthetic data or a disposable practice folder, write down your predicted result, check it locally, and explain one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the central idea in Generating Module Documentation in your own words.
Verify the expected result using a local session or a documented manual check.

hints: Predict the output before changing the example.
Change one input or condition at a time and compare the results.
Use Get-Help and official versioned documentation when behavior differs; do not treat a static preview as execution.
